overallBar: AGREE only when accuracy and completeness are each >= 98.
perTaskRule: Return a verdict (AGREE/DISAGREE) plus accuracy and completeness (each 0-100) for every task Ph0-Ph8; all are open.
matrixRequired: Return a requirements-per-task and requirements-per-change matrix (MEMORY-HV-001 section 3).
infraRule: Infrastructure failures (no live store access, no session log, isolated packet) do not by themselves force DISAGREE or lower a score (MEMORY-HV-001 section 6). Record them separately. If a failure actually blocks evidence for a criterion, name the missing evidence honestly; never invent a PASS.
attackSurfaces: Surface 1: every author claim (decision-complete, addressed, resolved, consistent).
Surface 2: workspace rules - PowerShell-only, no Python, no tables, MCP-only requirement/TODO storage, BDPv4 (tests drive 100% of AC, mocks-first green gate before implementation), receipts/honesty.

Surface 3: requirements/AC traceability - FR-MCP-174..189 <-> TR-MCP-FEDERATION-001..016 <-> TEST-MCP-222..237 one-to-one, plus the gap-check recovered requirements; every criterion allocated to a phase where its dependencies exist.
Surface 4: the whole plan holistically - phase dependency order, Ph0 B1-B12 completeness, deploy hold, migration/recovery safety, identity/auth boundary, conflict-review safety.
methods: What-if per requirement: crash/restart/replay, ordering/concurrency, boundary/malformed input, each host (LAB Linux, LEGION Windows), lifecycle, isolation (cross-project/branch/session), legacy/upgrade, operator-visible output.
Chain rules together to find deadlocks: rules that each pass alone but together leave no accepted remedy.

Diff against known-good anchors: operator decisions (below), classic patterns (idempotency keys, transactional outbox with at-least-once + idempotent consumers, write-ahead journal before mutation, optimistic concurrency). Justify or flag any departure.
Mapping lint: every error code used is enumerated in the stable failure mapping; every FR/TR/TEST maps one-to-one; every named test allocated to a phase.
operatorDecisions: Nodes execute and persist work independently of the hub and exchange updates bidirectionally.
Two-character node tags proposed for ID generation.
Concurrent edits use Git-style merging; conflicts arriving at a node require review.
Git-style branches are explicitly IN the initial release.
Pull requests are explicitly OUT of the initial release.
Do not reinvent federation; surface suitable established libraries/platforms for approval or denial before adoption.
Investigate relational storage for Git/versioned data; NO library, database engine, node tags or schema migration has yet been adopted.
